1 · Rollen en toegang (5)

▶ INC-78

Rolgebaseerde flags voor tekening downloaden en klantnaam zien

3 Points In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Rollen en toegang · Inschatting: M

Waarom

Bijna alle verschillen tussen rollen komen neer op twee instellingen: mag iemand de tekening downloaden, en mag iemand de klantnaam zien. Door dit als losse flags per rol te bouwen kun je later schuiven zonder het rolmodel opnieuw te ontwerpen.

Detail

De klantnaam moet verdwijnen uit zowel de list view als de detail view, maar filteren op klant blijft wel mogelijk. Download moet op API-niveau geblokkeerd zijn, niet alleen verstopt in de UI.

“Er zijn eigenlijk maar 2 dingen die onderscheidend zijn: tekening downloaden en de klantnaam.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

Currently roles flow from Azure AD into session at api/main.py login_callback (lines 611-634) and are exposed read-only via GET /api/auth/me (lines 463-483). There is NO authorization: RequireLoginMiddleware (line 181) only checks user presence, is_public_path (line 150) only gates login. The DXF endpoint download_dxf at line 2471 has zero role check. Klant/customer is selected as 'customer' in the profile SQL (lines 844, 1249, 2135) and serialized in every response model, then shown in list/detail in app/page.tsx (line 3114 badge, getDisplayCustomer line 70). Target: derive two boolean capability flags (can_download_dxf, can_see_customer) from session roles server-side, strip customer from API payloads when false, and hard-block download_dxf with 403 when false, while keeping the customer filter (WHERE Klant) working.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Add a role-to-capabilities map and helper get_capabilities(user) in api/main.py near is_public_path, e.g. ROLE_FLAGS = {Engineering: {dxf:True, customer:True}, SalesSupport:{dxf:False,customer:True}, Sales:{dxf:False,customer:False}, ...}; union flags across the user roles list from session.
  2. Add a FastAPI dependency require_capability(flag) (Depends on request.session user) returning 403 when the flag is false; apply it to download_dxf at line 2471 so download is blocked at API level, not just UI.
  3. Extend GET /api/auth/me (line 471 safe_user) to also return capabilities so the frontend can hide UI affordances without being the security boundary.
  4. In the profile SQL serialization paths (/api/profiles ~line 1081, /api/profiles/{id} ~line 1360, search-by-image ~line 1738/2164), after building the response objects, blank/remove the customer field when get_capabilities(user).customer is False; keep the WHERE Klant filter logic (lines 931, 1181) untouched so filtering by customer still works server-side.
  5. In app/page.tsx read capabilities from /api/auth/me (extend CurrentUser at line 2284), guard the DXF button render (line 3190 area) and the customer Badge (line 3114) behind these flags, and disable downloadDxf() (line 977) optimistically.
  6. Keep the MultiSelect customer filter (line 2630) populated from /api/filters even when can_see_customer is false, so Sales can still filter by a customer they pick from the list without seeing it on results.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • The customer filter must keep working server-side even when the name is hidden client-side, so stripping must happen only on the response objects, never on the WHERE clause params.
  • Azure AD app role strings must be mapped exactly; if the Entra app registration emits display names vs role values the ROLE_FLAGS keys will silently miss and default to no access.
  • Hiding customer in the JSON but leaving it in the DXF filename or in stam_bedrijfsnaam/getDisplayCustomer (page.tsx line 70) could leak the name; all derived customer fields and the detail view must be covered.
  • LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT mock user (line 191) has no roles, so dev must default to full capabilities or testing role gating becomes impossible.
  • download_dxf accepts a raw article_number with no auth context today; adding the dependency must not break the existing blob lookup fallback path.

Diagram

flowchart TD
  A[Azure AD login] --> B[session user roles]
  B --> C[get_capabilities]
  C --> D{can download}
  D -->|no| E[block dxf 403]
  D -->|yes| F[serve dxf]
  C --> G{can see customer}
  G -->|no| H[strip customer from json]
  G -->|yes| I[include customer]
  H --> J[frontend list and detail]
  I --> J
▶ INC-79

Gebruikersbeheer view met enable/disable

5 Points Canceled

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Rollen en toegang · Inschatting: L

Waarom

Lassfom IT schoont vertrekkende medewerkers niet altijd netjes op, dus de PO wil zelf kunnen zien wie toegang heeft en accounts kunnen uitzetten. Aanmaken blijft bij IT via Entra, maar zichtbaarheid en disable komen in de tool.

Detail

De lijst toont naam, e-mail, rol, bron (intern of gast), laatste login en status. Gasten van externe tenants zoals Cimaboll en Cinobol staan naast de interne gebruikers.

“Jij kunt gewoon wel zeggen, deze gast die werkt hier niet meer, die staat hier wel in, dan gooi ik weer wat lucht.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

There is no user directory in the app today; the only persisted user record is tos_acceptances (created at api/main.py lines 392-406 with sub, email, name, oid, tid, roles, accepted_at). Login does not record last_login or a status flag. The frontend has no admin view. Target: a users table (or extend tos_acceptances) tracking name, email, role, source intern/gast, last_login, status enabled/disabled, a GET /api/admin/users list endpoint, a POST toggle endpoint, and an admin-only React view. Disable must actually block access in RequireLoginMiddleware, not just display.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Create a users table in init_db (alongside tos_acceptances creation ~line 392): columns sub PK, email, name, roles TEXT, source TEXT, last_login TEXT, status TEXT default 'enabled'.
  2. In login_callback (after line 627) upsert the user row and set last_login=now and derive source from tid (own tenant = intern, other tids like Cimaboll/Cinobol = gast).
  3. Add GET /api/admin/users and POST /api/admin/users/{sub}/status in api/main.py, both guarded by a require_role('Beheer') dependency; the list returns name, email, role, source, last_login, status.
  4. In RequireLoginMiddleware (line 239) after fetching the session user, look up the users table status and return 401/redirect to logout if status='disabled', so disabling takes effect on the next request.
  5. Build an admin users page/section in app/page.tsx (or a new route under app/) rendered only when currentUser.roles includes Beheer, showing a table with an enable/disable toggle calling the POST endpoint.
  6. Handle account creation staying with IT/Entra: the table is populated lazily on first login, so users who never logged in won't appear, document this behavior.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Disabled status only blocks on the NEXT request because the existing session cookie remains valid for max_age 3600 (line 270); to force-out you must also check status in middleware every request which adds a DB read per call.
  • Guests from external tenants (Cimaboll, Cinobol) have different tid values; mapping tid to a friendly source label requires a known tenant allowlist.
  • Users created in Entra but never logged in will be invisible since the table is login-populated; PO expectation of seeing all access may not be fully met without Graph API.
  • Concurrency: the per-request status lookup must use the existing get_db_connection pattern and not block; consider caching status in session at login but then disable won't be immediate.
  • Securing /api/admin/* requires the same role-mapping reliability as task one; a missing Beheer role mapping locks everyone out.

Diagram

flowchart TD
  A[user login] --> B[upsert users row]
  B --> C[set last login and source]
  D[Beheer opens admin view] --> E[GET api admin users]
  E --> F[table name email role source status]
  F --> G[toggle disable]
  G --> H[POST status disabled]
  H --> I[middleware blocks next request]
▶ INC-80

Aparte Customer Service rol

1 Point In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Rollen en toegang · Inschatting: S

Waarom

Customer Service krijgt voorlopig dezelfde rechten als de accountmanagers, maar de PO wil het toch als aparte rol omdat hij verwacht de rechten later te willen aanpassen.

“Misschien later anders, omdat ik misschien later de rechten wil aanpassen.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

Roles are free-form strings parsed from the Azure 'roles' claim (api/main.py line 612) with no enumerated set anywhere. Task one introduces the ROLE_FLAGS map. Target: add 'CustomerService' as a distinct key in that map that currently mirrors the Sales capability set (no dxf, per the matrix Sales sees no customer, but the matrix task says Customer Service spiegelt Sales), so it can later be edited independently without touching code structure.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Add a 'CustomerService' entry to the ROLE_FLAGS capability map in api/main.py with the same values as 'Sales' for now (a literal copy, not an alias, so it is independently tunable later).
  2. Confirm the corresponding Azure AD app role value 'CustomerService' is requested from IT to be added to the Entra app registration appRoles, since the claim string must match the map key exactly.
  3. Ensure get_capabilities unions correctly if a user holds both Sales and CustomerService roles (most-permissive union).
  4. Expose the resolved role/capabilities in /api/auth/me so the frontend and admin view (other tasks) display CustomerService distinctly.
  5. Add a unit-style check or seed in eval/test to assert CustomerService maps to expected flags so a future divergence from Sales is intentional.
  6. Document in CLAUDE.md/notes that CustomerService is intentionally a separate key duplicating Sales for now.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • The Entra app registration appRoles must include the exact 'CustomerService' value or the claim never arrives; this is an external IT dependency, not a code change alone.
  • Copy-paste of Sales flags risks future drift; without a test asserting the intended divergence point, a refactor could silently re-merge them.
  • If a user has both Sales and CustomerService, union semantics must be defined now to avoid surprising escalation later.
  • No DB-level role storage exists, so role changes are entirely driven by the Entra claim; the app cannot grant CustomerService itself.

Diagram

flowchart TD
  A[Entra appRoles CustomerService] --> B[roles claim]
  B --> C[session roles]
  C --> D[ROLE_FLAGS lookup]
  D --> E[CustomerService entry copy of Sales]
  E --> F[capabilities]
  F --> G[independently tunable later]
▶ INC-81

Volledige rolmatrix: Engineering, Sales Support, Sales, Customer Service, Beheer

3 Points In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Rollen en toegang · Inschatting: M

Waarom

De vijf rollen zijn in de eerste sessie vastgesteld. Engineering mag alles, Sales Support mag alles behalve tekeningen downloaden, Sales ziet geen klantnaam, Customer Service spiegelt Sales, en Beheer krijgt statistieken en gebruikersbeheer.

Detail

Entra ID blijft de identiteitsbron. De rolmatrix wordt binnen de tool toegepast bovenop de Entra-accounts.

Code-analyse

This is the umbrella consolidating tasks one to three. Today roles are parsed (line 612) but nothing enforces a five-role matrix; Engineering=all, SalesSupport=all except dxf download, Sales=no customer name, CustomerService=mirrors Sales, Beheer=statistics + user management. Target: a single authoritative capability matrix in api/main.py keyed by these five Entra role strings, driving the dxf gate (task one), customer stripping (task one), admin/stats access (task two and the Gebruiksstatistieken section), all on top of Entra identity which remains the source of truth.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Define the canonical ROLE_FLAGS matrix in api/main.py with all five roles and the columns: can_download_dxf, can_see_customer, can_access_admin, can_view_stats; Engineering all true, SalesSupport dxf false others true, Sales customer false dxf false, CustomerService = Sales, Beheer admin+stats true.
  2. Implement get_capabilities(user) computing the most-permissive union across the user's Entra roles, with a safe default (no capabilities, or full in LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT only).
  3. Wire require_capability/require_role dependencies onto download_dxf (line 2471), the future admin/users endpoints, and the future usage-stats endpoints so every gated surface reads from this one matrix.
  4. Apply customer-field stripping in the profile serialization paths based on can_see_customer (shared with task one).
  5. Surface capabilities in /api/auth/me (line 471) and consume them in app/page.tsx to hide DXF buttons, customer badges, admin and stats views per role.
  6. Add a small README/test enumerating the matrix so changes to one role are reviewed against the whole table; coordinate the five role values with IT for the Entra appRoles definitions.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Entra remains identity source: the five role VALUE strings in the app must exactly match the appRoles configured in the Azure app registration, an external coordination point.
  • Most-permissive union means a user accidentally assigned both Sales and Engineering in Entra gets full access; the matrix cannot fix mis-assignment, only IT can.
  • A wrong default (fail-open) would expose customer names and DXF to unmapped roles; must fail-closed in production while staying usable in LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.
  • The matrix touches many endpoints (search, detail, image-search, dxf, future admin/stats); missing one serialization path leaks customer data.
  • Future per-role tuning (PO explicitly expects to change CustomerService) must remain a one-line matrix edit, so all enforcement must read the matrix, never hardcode role checks inline.

Diagram

flowchart TD
  A[Entra identity five roles] --> B[session roles]
  B --> C[ROLE_FLAGS matrix]
  C --> D[capabilities union]
  D --> E[dxf gate]
  D --> F[customer visibility]
  D --> G[admin access]
  D --> H[stats access]
  E --> I[endpoints and frontend]
  F --> I
  G --> I
  H --> I
▶ INC-140

Terms & Conditions accreditering bij inloggen (per-clausule vinkjes + accept all)

5 Points In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Rollen en toegang · Inschatting: L · Bron: e-mail Koen & Marco (rollout User Management)

Waarom

In relatie tot User Management is één aspect vergeten. In fase 1 is hiervoor al een knop gemaakt maar niet uitgewerkt. Nu de tool verder uitgerold wordt, is het belangrijk dat de Terms & Conditions accreditering geregeld wordt. Destijds zijn er een aantal Poppe-medewerkers aan de tool toegevoegd die hiervoor een individuele overeenkomst getekend hebben; dit moet nu in de tool zelf afgedwongen worden.

Detail

Bij inloggen moet een medewerker een aantal vinkjes zetten alvorens hij verder kan, inclusief een "accept all"-vinkje. Acceptatie moet geregistreerd worden (wie, wanneer, welke versie) en de toegang moet geblokkeerd blijven tot er geaccepteerd is. Dit is een rollout-blocker voor nieuwe locaties/gebruikers.

Terms & Conditions (te tonen)

Non-Disclosure / confidentiality Agreement for the use of an AI-assisted "Elastofirm Profiler Tool" within the Elastofirm Group The AI-supported application "Elastofirm Profiler Tool" gives authorized employees of the Elastofirm Group access to profile and/or tool drawings and customer data of products, including from other factories within the Elastofirm Group, via software and app. It allows users to compare (new) projects within the other sites of the Elastofirm Group and to exchange information with responsible colleagues. The data and drawings provided in the software must be treated responsibly and confidentially by all users. Special attention should be paid to the following points:

De afzonderlijke clausules (elk een eigen verplicht vinkje):

  1. Only authorized employees within Elastofirm locations have access to the software. Users must ensure that no unauthorized employees or customers have access to the software or the data it contains.
  2. The use of the Software is only permitted after acceptance of this confidentiality agreement.
  3. Drawings, designs and data may not be copied, otherwise reproduced, or distributed.
  4. The rights of an article belong to the manufacturer who produces the product in question within the Elastofirm Group.
  5. Product and process related data may not be shared or published outside the Elastofirm Group.
  6. Customer-related data and information may not be disclosed or shared with third parties.
  7. The employee is informed that the data and content provided constitute sensitive information requiring protection.
By accepting these terms, the employee agrees to comply with these rules. If the employee has any questions regarding the use of the Tool, they should contact their supervisor or the administrator of the Tool.

Code-analyse

De TOS-infrastructuur bestaat al gedeeltelijk maar is niet afgemaakt. In api/main.py: ensure_tos_table() (regel 389) maakt tabel tos_acceptances (sub, email, name, oid, tid, roles, accepted_at, tos_version regel 394-406); TOS_VERSION env default "v2" (regel 110); GET /api/tos/status (regel 411) geeft accepted + required_version; POST /api/tos/accept (regel 432) schrijft één rij en zet request.session["tos_accepted"]. is_public_path laat /tos toe (regel 160). De frontend app/tos/page.tsx heeft echter maar één checked checkbox en roept accept onvoorwaardelijk aan; er zijn geen per-clausule vinkjes, geen accept-all, en de acceptatie wordt niet afgedwongen in de middleware (RequireLoginMiddleware gates alleen login, niet TOS — zie comment regel 256 "lets users accept voluntarily"). Target: per-clausule verplichte vinkjes + accept-all, harde gating tot geaccepteerd, versie ophogen naar v3 met deze tekst, en vastleggen welke clausules zijn afgevinkt.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Bump TOS_VERSION naar "v3" in api/main.py (regel 110) en leg de canonieke clausule-tekst vast (constante in de backend of een tos_clauses definitie) zodat versie en inhoud aan elkaar gekoppeld zijn.
  2. Breid tos_acceptances uit met een kolom accepted_clauses TEXT (JSON-lijst van clausule-ids) via een ALTER-migratie, zodat auditbaar is welke punten zijn afgevinkt; behoud bestaande rijen.
  3. Pas POST /api/tos/accept (regel 432) aan om de afgevinkte clausules in de body te valideren (alle verplichte clausules aanwezig) en op te slaan; weiger acceptatie als niet alle vinkjes gezet zijn.
  4. Forceer TOS-gating: in RequireLoginMiddleware (rond regel 256) na de login-check de tos_status voor de huidige required_version controleren en redirecten naar /tos?next=... als niet geaccepteerd (open redirect-guard: alleen paden die met / beginnen en niet met //).
  5. Werk app/tos/page.tsx uit: render de 7 clausules elk met een eigen verplicht vinkje, plus een "Accept all"-checkbox die alle vinkjes tegelijk zet/wist; de Verder/Akkoord-knop is disabled tot alle verplichte vinkjes aan staan.
  6. Stuur de afgevinkte clausule-ids mee in de POST /api/tos/accept body en redirect na succes naar next (zelfde veilige redirect-logica).
  7. Toon op een herhaalbezoek de reeds-geaccepteerde status + datum (uit /api/tos/status), en her-prompt automatisch wanneer required_version wijzigt (zodat een nieuwe versie iedereen opnieuw laat tekenen).
  8. (Optioneel, sluit aan op Gebruikersbeheer-issue) Toon in de admin-view wie welke TOS-versie wanneer accepteerde; markeer de reeds individueel getekende Poppe-medewerkers als geaccrediteerd (backfill een rij of een vrijstellingsvlag).

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Gating in de middleware mag de publieke paden (/tos, /auth/*, /_next/, /images/) niet blokkeren, anders ontstaat een redirect-loop op de TOS-pagina zelf.
  • LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT injecteert een mock-user zonder TOS-rij; dev moet TOS kunnen overslaan of een seed hebben, anders is lokaal testen geblokkeerd.
  • Versiebeheer: bij het ophogen naar v3 moeten álle gebruikers opnieuw accepteren; de status-check moet op exact required_version matchen, niet alleen op "bestaat een rij".
  • Juridische volledigheid: de getoonde tekst, de afzonderlijke clausules en de opgeslagen accepted_clauses moeten met de definitieve overeenkomst overeenkomen; tekstwijziging = nieuwe versie.
  • De reeds individueel getekende Poppe-medewerkers moeten niet dubbel hoeven tekenen of juist bewust wél opnieuw via de tool; dit is een productbeslissing die in de backfill verwerkt moet worden.

Diagram

flowchart TD
  A[User logs in] --> B[RequireLogin middleware]
  B --> C{tos accepted for required version}
  C -->|yes| D[Continue to app]
  C -->|no| E[Redirect to tos page with next]
  E --> F[Show 7 clauses each a checkbox]
  F --> G[Accept all toggles all]
  G --> H{all required checked}
  H -->|no| F
  H -->|yes| I[POST tos accept with clause ids]
  I --> J[Store row version and accepted_clauses]
  J --> D

2 · Gebruiksstatistieken (3)

▶ INC-82

Login en sessietellingen per gebruiker over 7/30/90 dagen

3 Points In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Gebruiksstatistieken · Inschatting: M

Waarom

De PO wil onderbouwd het gesprek aan kunnen gaan met afdelingen over tool-adoptie. Sales gebruikt de tool nog niet (logisch, ze hebben er geen doel op), en de engineers zijn jong en onervaren en zoeken te weinig voordat ze ontwerpen.

Detail

Het gaat niet om controle maar om bewijs. De PO noemt het verleidelijk om er statistieken bij te houden.

“Wekelijks constateer ik dat we dat niet doen. Hoe vaak wordt het gebruikt en door wie? Dat wil ik graag weten.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

Auth lives in api/main.py: the OAuth callback at /login/callback (line ~652) populates request.session['user'] with sub/name/email/oid/tid/roles. There is currently NO event logging: no table records logins, and the only per-user table is tos_acceptances (created in ensure_tos_table, line 389). The /api/auth/me endpoint (line 463) returns the current user. Target state: persist a row on each successful login (and ideally each authenticated API hit for 'sessions') into a new usage_events table, then expose an admin endpoint that aggregates counts per user over 7/30/90-day windows. The /download-csv handler (line 2541) already shows the admin-gating pattern (name startswith marco/auke) which can be reused for the stats endpoint.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Add ensure_usage_table() next to ensure_tos_table() in api/main.py creating table usage_events with columns id INTEGER PK, sub TEXT, email TEXT, name TEXT, event_type TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT datetime now, plus index on (sub, created_at); call it from startup_event() at line 2618.
  2. In the /login/callback handler (line ~652, right after request.session['user'] is set at line 627) insert one row with event_type='login' using sub/name/email from userinfo.
  3. Define a helper log_usage_event(session_user, event_type) that opens sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH) and inserts a row; guard with try/except so logging never breaks the request.
  4. In RequireLoginMiddleware.dispatch (line 181) after the user check passes, fire a lightweight event_type='session' insert at most once per session by setting request.session['session_logged_date'] to today (avoids a row per request).
  5. Add GET /api/admin/usage-stats endpoint that reuses the marco/auke name gate from /download-csv, runs GROUP BY sub with COUNT over WHERE created_at >= datetime now minus 7/30/90 days, returns JSON keyed by user.
  6. In app/page.tsx add an admin-only panel (gated on the roles/name already fetched via /api/auth/me at line 2299) that fetches /api/admin/usage-stats and renders a per-user table with the three windows.
  7. Bump version a minor per CLAUDE.md and verify LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT path (line 188) still works since it injects a mock user without going through the callback.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT bypass (line 188) never hits /login/callback, so logins are only recorded in production; dev testing needs a manual seed.
  • SQLite write on every authenticated request (session events) can cause write-lock contention under concurrency; mitigate with once-per-day-per-session dedupe and try/except.
  • Admin gate currently uses fragile name.startswith('marco'/'auke') string matching rather than the Azure roles claim; the roles claim mapping should ideally drive this but app roles may be empty.
  • DB_PATH may point at elastofirm-index-128.db which is rebuilt on reindex; usage_events must live in a DB that is NOT wiped by import_csv.py / reindex, otherwise history is lost.

Diagram

flowchart TD
 A[User login via Azure AD] --> B[login callback sets session user]
 B --> C[insert login row usage_events]
 D[Authenticated request] --> E[RequireLogin middleware]
 E --> F[once per day insert session row]
 C --> G[usage_events table]
 F --> G
 G --> H[admin usage-stats endpoint]
 H --> I[admin panel in page tsx]

▶ INC-83

Zoekintensiteit indicator (searches per sessie, filters toegepast)

3 Points In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Gebruiksstatistieken · Inschatting: M

Waarom

Alleen inloggen zegt weinig, want als je inlogt en niets doet heb je toch uren staan. De PO wil onderscheid tussen openen en echt gebruiken.

“Als je inlogt en je doet niks dan heb je natuurlijk heel veel uren.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

Searches are driven from app/page.tsx: searchProfiles() (line 336) calls GET /api/profiles, getProfilesCount() (line 367) calls /api/profiles/count, and image search calls /api/profiles/search-by-image (line 1439). The main search effect runs around line 1697. Currently nothing records that a search happened or which filters were applied; the backend /api/profiles endpoint (line 804) receives all filter params (query, industry, compound, customer, process_type, weight_min/max, surface_min/max, mold, department, etc) but logs only debug prints. Target: count search events and number of filters applied per session, distinguishing 'opened but idle' from 'actively searching', feeding the same usage_events table from the previous task with event_type='search' and a filters_count integer.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Extend usage_events table (or add a sibling search_events table) with columns filters_count INTEGER and had_query INTEGER in ensure_usage_table().
  2. In /api/profiles handler (api/main.py line 804) compute filters_count by counting non-None of the Query params, and after building results call log_usage_event with event_type='search' plus filters_count; do the same in /api/profiles/search-by-image (line 1678).
  3. Avoid double counting: /api/profiles and /api/profiles/count fire together (page.tsx line 1696-1698), so only instrument /api/profiles, not /api/profiles/count.
  4. Add an aggregation to GET /api/admin/usage-stats: searches per session computed as COUNT(event_type=search) divided by COUNT(DISTINCT session-day) per user, plus average filters_count, so idle logins show low intensity.
  5. In app/page.tsx surface an intensity figure in the admin panel (searches per session, avg filters applied), reusing the fetch added for the login-stats task.
  6. Pass a stable per-session id (store request.session['sid'] generated once in middleware) so searches can be grouped into sessions rather than only by day.
  7. Bump version a minor.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Distinguishing a real session boundary in a cookie-session app is fuzzy; using a generated session sid persisted in the session cookie is the most reliable grouping key.
  • React strict-mode / effect re-runs in page.tsx can fire the search effect twice on mount, inflating counts; the AbortController flow at line 1697 helps but server-side dedupe by sid+params hash may be needed.
  • Counting filters_count from Query params must stay in sync if new filters are added later (process, compound2, treatments tasks), otherwise the metric silently undercounts.

Code-analyse

There is an existing CSV download pattern at /download-csv (api/main.py line 2541) using fastapi.responses.Response with Content-Disposition attachment and the marco/auke admin gate, but it streams the source rubbermolds CSV from Azure Blob, not usage data. Implementatie stappen

  1. Add GET /api/admin/usage-export endpoint in api/main.py reusing the marco/auke (or roles) admin gate copied from /download-csv at line 2553.

  3. Serialize with csv.writer into io.StringIO and return fastapi Response(content=..., media_type='text/csv', headers Content-Disposition attachment filename=usage-export.csv), mirroring lines 2567-2571.
  4. Add an Export usage CSV button in the admin panel in app/page.tsx that hits the endpoint with credentials include (same pattern as the DXF download at line 1008).
  5. Ensure the export endpoint path is NOT added to is_public_path (line 150) so auth is enforced.
  6. Bump version a minor.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Privacy requirement is explicit: the export must exclude search query/filter content; schema and SELECT must guarantee no query text column is ever populated or exported.
  • Admin gate relies on name string matching which is brittle; ideally switch to the Azure roles claim (session user roles) but those may be unset for most accounts.
  • If usage_events is empty (feature just deployed or in LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT where logins are bypassed) the export is blank, which can look like a bug; add a header row always.
  • CSV encoding/locale: Dutch names with diacritics need utf-8 with BOM for Excel to render correctly, otherwise beheer sees garbled characters.

Coextrusie similarity met compound swap herkenning

8 Points Backlog

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Zoeken en similarity · Inschatting: XL

Waarom

Bij coextrusie wil je dat twee profielen met dezelfde geometrie maar omgewisselde kleurhuidjes nog steeds matchen. Dit is algoritme-werk en vraagt waarschijnlijk eerst een spike.

Detail

De PO verwacht dat je dit straks anders gaat willen dan nu, met echte coextrusie-matching op elkaar.

Code-analyse

Current similarity is pure HOG geometry cosine in api/image_search.py with PCA reduction (elastofirm-pca-128.pkl), and it has no notion of compound layers or color skins. Coextrusion requires that two profiles with identical geometry but swapped color skins still match. This is algorithm work: the HOG vector already captures geometry, but compound/skin identity is metadata in Compoundcode (and the future compound2). Target: a spike to define a combined similarity that treats geometry as primary and treats swapped compound2 assignments as equivalent.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Run a spike: analyze whether HOG geometry alone already matches swapped-skin coextrusion pairs, using known coextrusion article pairs from the dataset
  2. Define a compound-swap equivalence: treat a profile pair as compound-equivalent if their Compoundcode and Compoundcode2 sets are equal regardless of order
  3. Prototype a re-ranking layer in image_search.py that, after HOG cosine ranking, boosts or merges results whose geometry similarity is high and whose compound multiset matches the query (when query metadata is known)
  4. Decide where query metadata comes from since image search starts from an uploaded image with no compound; likely this matching applies in profile-to-profile mode not image-upload mode
  5. Add a similarity mode flag to /api/profiles/search-by-image or a new profile-to-profile endpoint that incorporates compound-swap logic
  6. Document findings and gate the feature behind the compound2 datamodel work; bump version a minor when shipped

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Image upload provides no compound metadata so swap recognition only works in profile-anchored similarity, not raw image search
  • Requires compound2 to exist first, so this is blocked on the compound 2 datamodel task
  • Defining the right blend of geometric similarity and compound equivalence risks over-merging visually distinct profiles; needs labeled coextrusion pairs to validate

Diagram

flowchart TD
A[anchor profile geometry] --> B[HOG cosine candidates]
B --> C[compute compound multiset]
C --> D{compound sets equal ignoring order}
D -->|yes| E[treat as coextrusion match]
D -->|no| F[rank by geometry only]
E --> G[merged similarity results]
F --> G

Fix: zoeken op alleen industrie geeft nu "no products found"

1 Point In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Zoeken en similarity · Inschatting: S

Waarom

Live gereproduceerde bug. Zoeken op alleen industrie geeft niets terug, maar zodra je een extra criterium toevoegt komen er wel resultaten. Dat is niet logisch.

“Industrie, agri, en dan zegt hij helemaal niks. Als ik nog iets toevoeg dan krijg ik ze wel. Dat is niet logisch.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

At SQL level industry-only works: LOWER(TRIM(Branche))=LOWER(TRIM('Agri')) returns 159 valid rows in elastofirm.db. The API /api/profiles and /api/profiles/count apply industry exact-match (lines 918-929 and 1168-1179). The bug surfaces only when industry is the sole criterion. The most likely cause is a mismatch between the dropdown value sent from /api/filters and the stored Branche, or that performSearch is not invoked when only a MultiSelect changes (handleSearch must be explicitly triggered) combined with the exact-equality being stricter than the LIKE used by other filters. Adding another criterion changes the matching path which is why results then appear.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Reproduce by calling /api/profiles?industry=Agri and /api/profiles/count?industry=Agri directly and compare counts to the 159 SQL baseline to confirm whether the bug is API or frontend
  2. If API returns 159 then the bug is frontend: verify industryFilter is correctly joined and sent as the industry param in performSearch (line 1572) and that the value matches the exact Branche casing from /api/filters
  3. Make industry matching consistent and forgiving: change the single-value industry condition from strict equality to the same normalized comparison used everywhere, and ensure leading/trailing whitespace and case are trimmed on both sides (already TRIM/LOWER) and trim the value sent by the frontend
  4. Check that selecting only an industry MultiSelect still triggers handleSearch; if the search only runs on the Search button, ensure the industry-only path reaches performSearch
  5. Add a regression test calling the endpoint with only industry=Agri asserting count 159
  6. Bump version a minor

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Exact equality breaks if the dropdown option carries extra characters or a trailing space that does not exist in the stored Branche; the LIKE-based filters mask this which is why adding a second criterion appears to fix it
  • If the frontend sends the wrong query param name or an empty string the API silently returns the full set, not zero, so the zero-result symptom points to a value mismatch not a missing param
  • Count and list endpoints must be fixed together or the header count and the grid will disagree

Diagram

flowchart TD
A[select only industry agri] --> B[performSearch industry param]
B --> C[api profiles exact match branche]
C --> D{value matches stored branche}
D -->|mismatch trailing space| E[zero results no products found]
D -->|trimmed normalized| F[159 results]
E --> G[fix trim and normalize]
G --> F

Veld "toepassing" met dropdown plus vrije invoer

3 Points In Review

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Toepassing en omschrijving · Inschatting: M

Waarom

De PO wil producten kunnen koppelen aan een toepassing of industrie, bijvoorbeeld industriedeuren of ramen en deuren. Een combinatie van bestaande waarden (dropdown) en het toevoegen van nieuwe.

“Dit is een voor ramen en deuren. Hoort bij ramen en deuren.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

The live profiles table (queried in api/main.py around line 835) uses CamelCase Dutch columns and has NO toepassing column; data/import_csv.py CREATE TABLE also lacks it. /api/filters (line 1500) builds dropdowns via SELECT DISTINCT on existing columns, and the frontend MultiSelect (app/page.tsx line 510) renders them. Target: add a new toepassing TEXT column, expose distinct values via /api/filters, and add a combobox (dropdown of existing values plus free text) in the detail panel and bulk panel. Because the app is currently read-only there is also no write path yet, so this depends on a new PATCH endpoint.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Add toepassing TEXT to the profiles CREATE TABLE in data/import_csv.py and write a migration script (e.g. scripts/add-classification-columns.py) that runs ALTER TABLE profiles ADD COLUMN toepassing TEXT on elastofirm-index-128.db / profiles.db
  2. Add Toepassing as toepassing (or the new column alias) to the SELECT in get_profiles (main.py ~835) and get_profile (~1253), and add the field to the Profile / ProfileWithDetails Pydantic models (~727)
  3. Extend /api/filters (main.py 1500) with a SELECT DISTINCT toepassing block returning filters["toepassings"], excluding NULL/empty
  4. Create a new PATCH endpoint PATCH /api/profiles/{id} in main.py that UPDATEs the toepassing column for one article (guarded by the data-management capability flag from the toggle task)
  5. In app/page.tsx add a creatable combobox component (extend MultiSelect or add a Combobox) bound to filterOptions.toepassings that allows selecting an existing value or typing a new one
  6. Wire the combobox onChange to call the PATCH endpoint, and add toepassing to the FilterOptions interface (page.tsx ~389) and the searchParams handling so it can also be used as a filter

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Schema mismatch: import_csv.py defines a snake_case schema but the deployed DB uses CamelCase Dutch columns, so the ALTER must target the actual deployed column naming and both DB files
  • Free-text entries fragment the distinct list (typos create near-duplicate options), so normalisation/trim and possibly a canonical lookup are needed
  • Re-import from rubbermolds-output.csv could drop the new column unless the importer is made to preserve/merge existing toepassing values
  • No existing write auth boundary, so the PATCH must not be callable by read-only users

Voor power-gebruik: shift-klik om een reeks records in één keer te selecteren. De PO kent shift-klik en accepteert dat het iets voor de handige gebruiker is.

“Shift klik voor multi-select? Ja, oké.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

Building on click-to-select, the PO wants shift-click range selection. The card list is rendered from the results array in app/page.tsx; each card knows its profile but not its index in the current render order. Target: track a lastSelectedIndex and on shift-click select the contiguous range between lastSelectedIndex and the clicked index, adding all to the selection Map.

  2. Add lastSelectedIndex state (number|null) to RubberProfileFinder
  3. In the card onClick, detect event.shiftKey; if true and lastSelectedIndex is set, compute the min/max range and add every profile in that slice of the current results array to the selection Map
  4. On a normal (non-shift) click, set lastSelectedIndex to the clicked index after toggling
  5. Disable native text selection on the result grid during shift-click via user-select none to avoid highlighting text
  6. Ensure the range uses the same key (profile.selector) used everywhere else in the selection Map

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • The current results array is paginated/limited, so a range cannot cross pages; range is only within the loaded set
  • Index stability: if results refetch mid-interaction the indices shift and the range becomes wrong, so lastSelectedIndex must reset on new search
  • Shift-click triggers browser text selection which must be suppressed
  • Interaction with the new click-to-select toggle semantics (shift should add to, not toggle, the range)

  2. Add the capability boolean to the /api/auth/me response so the frontend knows whether to show edit affordances

Profile upload (SVG/DXF/image)

5 Points Backlog

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Heatmap module (apart product) · Inschatting: L

Waarom

De ingang van de stroomingsleer-tool. Je uploadt een profiel-doorsnede waarop de heatmap berekend wordt. Er bestaat al een werkend prototype.

“Je kan zeggen van upload een profieltje.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

A working prototype already exists at artifacts/heatmap-designer.html: loadFile() uses createImageBitmap + an offscreen canvas, grayscale-binarizes to a Uint8Array (gray[i] = g<128?0:255) and feeds initCanvasWith(). It only accepts raster (PNG/JPG/BMP/GIF), never SVG or DXF. The backend already has POST /api/upload/process-image (calls preprocess_uploaded_image in shape_extractor.py, returns a normalized data:image/png base64) and explicitly rejects CAD via is_cad_file(). Target: make this a standalone Next.js route/page (e.g. app/heatmap/page.tsx) reusing the prototype JS, and accept SVG (rasterize client-side) and DXF (server-side via process_cad_file, gated by HAS_CAD_PROCESSING). DXF download already works through GET /api/download-dxf/{article} + azure_blob_client.find_dxf_by_article_number, so a profile can be pulled straight from the catalog into the heatmap.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Create app/heatmap/page.tsx as a client component and port the prototype script from artifacts/heatmap-designer.html (state, loadFile, initCanvasWith, recompute) into a React-friendly module under app/heatmap/lib/.
  2. Add SVG support in loadFile: detect file.type==='image/svg+xml', draw the SVG into an offscreen canvas via an Image element before the grayscale/binarize loop.
  3. Add DXF support: when extension is .dxf/.dwg, POST to a new or existing backend route that runs process_cad_file (guarded by HAS_CAD_PROCESSING at api/main.py:2209) and returns a normalized PNG, then binarize that PNG client-side.
  4. Reuse POST /api/upload/process-image so raster uploads go through preprocess_uploaded_image for consistent hole-preserving normalization instead of the raw client binarize.
  5. Add an entry point from the catalog: a Send to heatmap button on a profile card in app/page.tsx that fetches the profile image (or DXF via /api/download-dxf) and navigates to /heatmap with it preloaded.
  6. Add a max-file-size guard (10MB, matching the backend) and unsupported-format error toast mirroring app/page.tsx:1289.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • DXF is vector with no inherent fill/scale; process_cad_file must produce a closed filled silhouette or the EDT mask buildMask() in the prototype will be wrong.
  • HAS_CAD_PROCESSING is currently disabled in the deployed env (api/main.py shows a fallback), so DXF may need the dependency re-enabled or a documented limitation.
  • SVG with strokes-only (no fill) binarizes to outlines, producing a hollow mask; need fill-rule handling.
  • Auth: the standalone heatmap page is still behind RequireLoginMiddleware unless added to is_public_path; cross-fetching /images and /api/download-dxf requires credentials include.

▶ INC-127

Heatmap overlay rood-naar-blauw

3 Points Backlog

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Heatmap module (apart product) · Inschatting: M

Waarom

Visualiseert waar de rubberstroom het snelst is. Rood waar veel rubber omheen zit en de stroom snel is, blauw waar het dun is en de stroom zwak. De matrijs moet dat inverse compenseren: rood knijpen, blauw openen.

“Rood is dan waar de flow van de rubber het snelst is. Waar het zo blauw mogelijk is moet je het vergroten.” — Product owner, uit transcript

Code-analyse

The prototype recompute() in heatmap-designer.html computes a signed/Euclidean distance transform (edt2d, Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher) over the rubber mask from buildMask(), normalizes dist/maxD into t, and colors with a turbo-ish colormap (turboStops, blauw 0.0 -> geel/rood 1.0). Currently THICK rubber (large distance to boundary) = rood and THIN = blauw, which already matches the PO intent: rood = waar veel rubber omheen zit (snelle flow), blauw = dun (zwakke flow). Target: make the semantics explicit and add the inverse-compensation read (rood knijpen, blauw openen) as a derived advice layer, plus a true red-to-blue ramp option since the PO literally says rood-naar-blauw.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Add a colormap selector in the controls of heatmap-designer.html / the ported page: keep turbo and add a 2-stop blue->red ramp keyed on the same normalized t.
  2. Confirm orientation in recompute(): t = dist/maxD so thick=1=rood; document this inline so the inverse-mold logic is unambiguous.
  3. Add a derived compensation overlay: for each pixel compute a suggested mold-gap delta proportional to (0.5 - t), rendering knijpen on rood zones and openen on blauw zones as a faint contour or arrow field.
  4. Expose a legend update (already present at lines ~413-418) so the swatches read thin/boundary blue to thickest red.
  5. Throttle recompute via the existing scheduleRecompute() requestAnimationFrame path when toggling colormap to avoid recomputing the EDT needlessly (colormap change only needs a re-render, not a new edt2d).

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • edt2d is O(W*H) per recompute; re-running it on every colormap toggle is wasteful, so cache the dist Float32Array and only re-render the canvas on colormap change.
  • maxD normalization makes color relative per-profile, so two profiles are not comparable in absolute mm; may need a fixed physical scale.
  • The inverse compensation (rood knijpen) is qualitative; turning it into actual mold-gap numbers needs material flow constants the PO has not provided yet.

Code-analyse

This is already partially built. recompute() in heatmap-designer.html (lines ~1037-1059) has an outline overlay gated by state.showOutline and the #outline-toggle checkbox (checked by default). It detects edges by 4-neighbour difference on the binarized imageData and paints white pixels (255,255,255, alpha 180) onto heatmapOverlay. Implementatie stappen

  1. Separate outer-contour detection from inner edges: run a connected-component / flood-fill from the canvas border to identify the outer void, then mark only pixels adjacent to that outer void as the outer contour.
  2. Render the outer contour at full alpha white with a slightly thicker stroke, and keep interior hole/core edges at the existing faint alpha (or a different color).
  3. Optionally compute the contour vector via the backend cv2.findContours hierarchy already used in shape_extractor.py (find_shape_hierarchy returns main_idx) and pass the outer polygon to the canvas for a clean anti-aliased stroke instead of per-pixel edges.
  4. Wire the existing #outline-toggle so it toggles outer-only vs all-edges.
  5. Ensure the white contour layers above the heatmap fill but below the inscribed circle (already the layering order in heatmapOverlay).

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • Per-pixel edge detection produces 1px jagged lines; a vector polyline from cv2 contours would look better but requires round-tripping to the backend on every drawing edit.
  • Distinguishing outer contour from holes requires the hierarchy; the current client code has no hierarchy, only a binary mask.
  • Drawing tools (draw/erase) mutate imageData live, so the outer contour must recompute on each paint stroke without lagging.

  • Orientation against the inloopband assumes a known down direction; the canvas has no gravity, so the user must pick or the system must test all rotations.
  • Deformation is a physical/material property (hardness, compound), data which lives in profiles.hardness/compound but is not linked to any mechanical model.

▶ INC-139

Optioneel later: dagelijkse order allocation recommender

8 Points Backlog

Open in Linear →

Sectie: Productielijn calculator (alleen voor operations) · Inschatting: XL

Waarom

De volgende stap zou zijn om de hele dagelijkse order-intake over alle lijnen te verdelen voor maximale gemiddelde utilisatie. Dat vereist wel live planningsdata om te weten welke lijnen vrij zijn.

Detail

Zonder integratie met het planningssysteem blijft het een calculator, geen recommender.

Code-analyse

The future step distributes the whole daily order intake across all lines for maximum average utilisation. The PO notes that without integration with the planning system it stays a calculator, not a recommender (no live data on which lines are free). The repo has no planning integration: external systems (SAP/BI) are mentioned only as systems of record. This builds on calc_line_options (per-article per-line metrics) and adds an optimization layer plus a NEW data feed of line availability. Target: an allocator that takes the day's orders plus live line availability and returns an assignment maximising utilisation.

Implementatie stappen

  1. Define the optimization problem: maximise average utilisation across lines subject to per-line capacity and order constraints.
  2. Build api/order_allocator.py using the per-line metrics from line_calculator and a solver (greedy first, then optionally an LP/assignment solver).
  3. Specify the planning data contract: which lines are free/occupied per shift, sourced from the planning system (likely via the BI/SQL layer or a new feed).
  4. Add POST /api/operations/allocate (role-gated like the calculator) accepting a list of order ids plus availability, returning the assignment.
  5. Build an operations-only allocation view in the frontend showing the recommended per-line schedule.
  6. Gate go-live on the planning integration; until then ship as a what-if calculator with manually entered availability.
  7. Bump version a minor.

Mogelijke uitdagingen

  • No planning system integration exists; without live line availability this cannot become a true recommender, exactly the PO's caveat.
  • Combinatorial allocation across 7 to 25 daily products over multiple lines needs a real solver; naive greedy may give clearly suboptimal schedules.
  • SAP/BI sync timing means availability data can be stale, producing recommendations that conflict with reality on the floor.
  • Same strict role gate must apply; an allocation view is even more commercially sensitive than the single-article calculator.
